limitations_of_naive_chunk_rag.description: Standard fixed-size chunking (e.g. 512 tokens with 64 overlap) slices through class definitions, functions, and cross-file import statements, breaking syntactic integrity.

limitations_of_naive_chunk_rag.limitation: Absence of Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) Graphs
limitations_of_naive_chunk_rag.description: Text embedding models evaluate lexical and surface semantic similarity rather than formal AST hierarchies (parent classes, method declarations, lexical scopes).

limitations_of_naive_chunk_rag.limitation: Inability to Traverse Cross-File Call Graphs
limitations_of_naive_chunk_rag.description: Questions like 'Which function calls X?' or 'Trace user upload through all files' require following directional call edges across 8-10 distinct files. Basic vector retrieval retrieves disjoint snippets without edge connectivity.

Configuration changes (e.g. EMBEDDING_DIMENSION 384 -> 768) propagate across multiple layers (DB schemas, model weights, vector index constraints). Text embeddings cannot infer database-to-vector-index type constraints.

sourcegraph_and_code_graph_advantages.description: Sourcegraph uses compiler-backed indexing (SCIP/LSIF) to provide 100% deterministic 'Find Definitions' and 'Find References' across thousands of files.
Combines structural pattern matching (AST regex) with semantic embeddings for syntax-aware code search.
Exposes explicit call graphs and dependency graphs to LLMs, replacing random top-K vector search with deterministic code path traversal.
